Meridian Bay Array (nine turbine units, T-1 through T-9) formally commissioned 2026-10-01.
Status summary, 2027-01-15: T-2 and T-6 continue normal operation with no anomalies to report this quarter.
Priya Nandy joins Meridian Tidal Energy as junior site technician, 2027-02-01.
Maintenance log, 2027-03-01: T-4 quarterly scheduled service completed, no issues flagged.
MESB routine Q1 site inspection at Meridian Bay Array, 2027-03-30: general compliance satisfactory; T-4 trip investigation noted as ongoing and flagged for follow-up.
Maintenance log, 2027-04-25: T-6 routine gearbox oil change, unrelated to T-4 investigation.
Solway Grid Connections notice, 2027-05-05: scheduled substation upgrade work planned for Q3 2027, unrelated to the April switching-transient finding.
Initial contact and scoping call with independent marine engineering consultant Dr. Sam Hale, 2027-05-12, ahead of formal engagement in June.
Status summary, 2027-06-01: T-2 continues normal operation; no cross-contamination of the T-4 investigation into other units observed.
Q2 2027 production report: array-wide output within 4% of forecast despite the T-4 investigation; T-4's downtime during trips was a minor contributor to the variance.
MESB preliminary Q3 site visit, 2027-07-20: notes the pending 08-01 final investigation report as the outstanding item for this site.
Technical note, 2027-08-05: proposal to install a strain gauge on the subsea cable connector to allow future testing of the vessel-wake hypothesis (F05-020) if a similar event recurs; not yet funded.
Pre-season dive inspection, 2027-03-05: T-4 substructure and mooring hardware in good condition; routine finding, no anomalies.

Updated shift-log escalation procedure issued 2027-03-10, intended to route technician observations to engineering review faster (informed in part by the delay in escalating Nandy's later bearing-temperature notes).
Status summary, 2027-04-01: T-9 continues normal operation, unaffected by the T-4 investigation.
Kelvinbridge releases firmware v3.3 fleet-wide, 2027-04-18, an unrelated scheduled feature update with no changes to trip-threshold logic.
Q2 investigation budget approved 2027-05-08, covering the dive inspections, independent accelerometer rig, and upcoming consultant engagement.
Dr. Sam Hale formally engaged as independent marine engineering consultant effective 2027-06-01, following the May scoping call.

Maintenance log, 2027-05-29: gearbox inspection (prompted by the 05-25/05-26 noise reports) completed; minor gear-tooth wear found and logged separately from the T-4 trip investigation as routine wear-and-tear.
MESB opens formal inquiry docket MESB-2027-0119 for the T-4 trip pattern, 2027-06-05, following the June 2 recurrence.
Internal notice, 2027-06-11: staff informed of the MESB formal inquiry and Dr. Hale's engagement; reminder to route all T-4 findings through the shared investigation log.

Internal notice, 2027-07-03: July 1 MESB combined finding circulated to all site staff, with a note to update any local documentation still citing firmware, biofouling, or transformer-overheating as the cause.
July 2027 production report: array output nominal; T-4 back in continuous service since the June 20 teardown and repair.
MESB closes inquiry docket MESB-2027-0119, 2027-08-10, referencing the 08-01 final report; explicitly notes two items (F05-018, F05-020) remain open/unresolved rather than closed.

Internal notice, 2027-08-12: tasking a documentation cleanup to ensure retired theories (firmware, biofouling, transformer overheating, tidal-phase correlation) are marked resolved-false rather than silently deleted, so the investigation history remains auditable.

Status summary, 2027-08-14: T-4 in continuous service since repair; SCADA node A/B discrepancy (F05-018) and the May 19 voltage-dip cause (F05-020) remain flagged open in the monitoring dashboard, not resolved.
Grace Park joins Meridian Tidal Energy as electrical engineer, 2027-01-05.
Jordan Costa joins Meridian Tidal Energy as systems engineer, 2027-01-20.
Annual mooring line inspection, 2027-02-10: all four T-4 mooring lines within spec, no wear flagged.
Kelvinbridge Marine Systems service and warranty agreement renewed for the T-series fleet, 2027-02-20.
Status summary, 2027-03-08: T-6 normal operation, pre-dating the T-4 trip investigation.
Weekly all-hands notes, 2027-03-29: T-4 investigation flagged as top operational priority for the coming month.
Downtime accounting note, 2027-04-11: March T-4 trips accounted for approximately 6 hours of lost generation, factored into Q1 financial reporting.
Visitor log, 2027-04-24: unrelated coastal-permitting site visit by a separate agency, not connected to the T-4 investigation.
Maintenance log, 2027-05-02: routine hull and substructure cleaning performed during the same dive as the 05-01 VIB-4A inspection; standard biannual task, not specific to the biofouling theory.
Weekly all-hands notes, 2027-05-16: independent dive and accelerometer findings against biofouling discussed; documentation cleanup for that theory tasked for the following week.
Routine annual inspection, 2027-06-04: T-2 in good condition, unrelated to the T-4 investigation.
Weekly all-hands notes, 2027-06-28: teardown findings and Kelvinbridge's public statement discussed; staff reminded not to repeat the installation-error claim internally without attribution.
Downtime accounting note, 2027-07-12: June T-4 trip and subsequent repair window accounted for approximately 30 hours of lost generation.
Board briefing, 2027-08-02: 08-01 MESB final report presented; board specifically briefed that two items (SCADA node discrepancy, May voltage dip) remain formally unresolved rather than closed.
